newsitem.title: GAMBIA: Gambians vote in parliamentary poll.
newsitem.headline: Gambians vote in parliamentary poll.

text.p: Gambians voted for a new parliament on Thursday in elections expected to consolidate the rule of President Yahya Jammeh who seized power in a coup in 1994 and won a disputed presidential poll last September.

With 107 candidates contesting 45 of parliament's 49 seats, early turnout was light although small queues formed in some areas. Most polling stations opened on time at 7 a.m. (0700 GMT), election officials said.
More than 446,000 of Gambia's one million or so people are registered to vote in the small West African nation which is heavily dependent on tourism.

The Alliance for Patriotic Reorientation and Construction (APRC), formed by Jammeh's supporters, is the only party contesting all 45 seats. It had already won five outright in constituencies where no one was standing against it.

Jammeh, who toppled independence leader Sir Dawda Jawara in 1994 accusing him of corruption, banned established politicians from politics before the presidential poll, denouncing their links with Jawara.

Opposition in the former British colony has since gathered around lawyer Ousainou Darboe and his United Democratic Party. Two minor opposition parties are also contesting seats along with six independents.
Polls close at 6 p.m. (1800 GMT). First results were expected on Thursday evening.
